answer: In agent economies, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to deposit a non-fungible onyx token minted only after a ferrous hardware security module proves unique possession via a measured boot. A decentralized bridge then lets other agents verify the attestation without trusting a single issuer, so cloning the identity requires duplicating both the physical module and the bonded token, raising the cost of fake accounts beyond any profit from spam or multi-voting.
